editorial.titleTr: Subway Strikes End...But Disabled Workers' Right to Move and Work Remains Non-Negotiable
summaryTr: The National Coalition for the Elimination of Discrimination Against People with Disabilities reached an agreement with the Seoul Metropolitan Council and ended their subway protest.
The rights to mobility and labor for people with disabilities were reflected in the ordinance bill and passed through the National Assembly.
Substantial budget support from the government and Seoul City is essential.
editorial.bodyTr: The National Coalition on Disability Discrimination Elimination has suspended its subway protests during morning commute hours following a major agreement with the Seoul Metropolitan Council. With provisions for securing disabled persons' right to mobility and labor rights now reflected in ordinance bills, and a disability rights protection bill having passed through the National Assembly, the government and Seoul city need to provide substantive budgetary policy support.

editorial.body: 정부가 경찰의 비대해진 권한과 수사 역량 한계에 따른 우려로 경찰 개혁 기구 신설을 지시함. 그러나 과거 검찰 수사권을 박탈해 사법 시스템의 상호 견제 기능을 약화시킨 정권이 이제야 개혁을 운운하는 것은 책임 회피라는 비판이 존재함.

editorial.titleTr: Editorial: Police Reform Now? Creating the Problem, Then Belated Medicine
summaryTr: The government has instructed the establishment of a new police reform body.
It is contradictory for the same administration that stripped the prosecution of investigative powers to now speak of reform.
Critics argue that this amounts to creating the disease and then belatedly prescribing the cure.
editorial.bodyTr: The government has instructed the establishment of a new police reform body amid concerns over the police force's bloated authority and limited investigative capabilities. However, there is criticism that a administration which previously stripped prosecutors of investigative powers, thereby weakening the mutual checks within the judicial system, is now speaking of reform as an attempt to shirk responsibility.

editorials.titleTr: [Editorial] Special Prosecutor Kwon Chang-young Put Politics Ahead of Investigation from Start to Finish
summaryTr: Special Prosecutor Kwon Chang-young concluded the investigation by indicting 58 people and handing over a case involving 150 people to police.
The move sparked controversy over politically charged remarks and unfounded allegations.
The lack of tangible investigative results has raised skepticism about the special prosecutor system.
editorials.bodyTr: The second independent counsel investigation into Kwon Chang-young concluded by indicting 58 individuals and referring cases involving the remaining 150 people to police. As the special prosecutor faced controversy over politically charged remarks and groundless allegations, criticism has mounted over the lack of substantive investigative results, raising doubts about the future of the independent counsel system itself.

editorials.titleTr: Editorial: Attempt to Punish Official for Contradicting President Halted—A Shabby Display
summaryTr: The court has canceled the suspension of director Park Ji-hyang from her duties.
The Education Ministry accused the Dokdo field trip of embezzlement, but failed to prove intent.
After the presidential remarks, there are concerns that the Education Ministry's excessive investigation was problematic.
editorials.bodyTr: The court has ordered the return of Park Ji-hyang, director of the Northeast Asian History Foundation, who had been suspended from duties by the Ministry of Education. The ministry had accused her of embezzlement related to a Dokdo research trip, but the court halted the action, citing insufficient evidence of willful misconduct. Director Park argues that the Education Ministry's excessive investigation following presidential remarks was the backdrop to this incident.

editorial.body: 입력 2026.08.12 00:14 2026.08.07 00:12 2026.06.04 00:41 이재명 대통령이 25일 청와대에서 열린 제37회 국무회의를 주재하고 있다. 청와대사진기자단 최근 일선 치안 현장에서 경찰의 심각한 무능과 무책임한 사건 처리 실태가 잇따라 드러나 충격을 주고 있다. 제주에서는 실종 신고가 접수됐음에도 경찰이 “연락이 닿았다”고 거짓말하고 사건을 종결하는 등 부실 대응 속에 시신이 계속 발견되고 있다. 광주에서도 여고생 살해사건과 관련해 경찰의 부실 수사와 조직적 증거 인멸 정황 등으로 시민들의 공분이 들끓었었다. 국민의 생명과 안전을 최전선에서 지켜야 할 경찰의 역량이 형편없이 낮고 내부 규율도 엉망이라는 점을 온 국민이 알게 된 상황이다. 국민이 생명을 잃는 등 심각한 부작용이 터져나오고 나서야 정부·여당은 뒤늦게 경찰 개혁을 거론하고 있다. 이재명 대통령은 어제 국무회의에서 “경찰이 국가기구 중 가장 큰 권력을 행사하게 될 것 같다”며 총리실에 경찰 개혁 기구를 주문했다. 민주당은 부랴부랴 경찰개혁추진단을 발족했다. 하지만 경찰의 수사 역량과 조직 내부 기강을 사전에 검증하거나 통제 장치를 두는 조치도 없이 경찰에 수사 전권을 부여하는 ‘검수완박’을 단행한 것이 정부·여당이다. 이제 와서 경찰의 역량과 기강 해이를 문제 삼아 쇄신을 주문하는 것은 일의 순서가 완전히 거꾸로 된 것이다. 이런 사태는 예견된 일이나 마찬가지다. 더불어민주당은 법조계와 학계·시민사회의 우려와 반대를 무시하고 검찰의 수사권을 완전 박탈하는 형사소송법 개정안을 입법 독주로 강행처리했다. 이에 따라 모든 수사를 경찰에 맡기면서 검찰의 보완수사권마저 두지 않아 경찰권 행사의 오남용을 견제하고 보완할 장치를 아예 없애버렸다. 약자가 피해를 볼 것이라는 경고를 무시하고 무리하게 추진한 입법의 결과가 지금 우리가 보고 있는 경찰의 부실 수사다. 국민이 바라는 것은 정치적 목적에 따른 제도 변화가 아니라 범죄로부터 안전하게 보호받는 일상이다. 실종사건의 허위 종결과 관련해 제주서부경찰서장 등이 대기발령됐는데, 서장을 문책하는 선에서 그칠 일이 아니다. 정부와 여당은 준비되지 않은 형사사법 개편이 초래한 부작용에 대해 돌아보고, 아직 시간이 있으니 검찰의 보완수사권을 되살리는 등 지금이라도 실질적인 보완 입법에 나서야 할 것이다.

editorial.titleTr: Police Negligence and Lax Discipline: Did They Not Know What Would Happen With Forced Prosecution Reform?
summaryTr: Police negligence and irresponsibility are repeatedly coming to light, putting citizens' lives at risk.
The government and ruling party are belatedly calling for police reform after pushing through the completion of prosecutorial investigation authority transfer.
Immediate legislation is needed to address the side effects of the unprepared criminal justice system overhaul.
editorial.bodyTr: Recent revelations of serious incompetence and irresponsible case handling by police at frontline law enforcement sites have shocked the nation. In Jeju, police falsely reported that contact had been made with a missing person and closed the case, yet bodies continue to be discovered amid bungled investigations. In Gwangju, public outrage erupted over police negligence in a high school girl's murder case and apparent systematic evidence destruction. Citizens nationwide now understand that police lack adequate capability to protect lives and safety at the frontline, and internal discipline is in shambles. Only after serious consequences including loss of life have emerged are the government and ruling party belatedly discussing police reform. President Lee Jae-myung ordered the Prime Minister's Office yesterday to establish a police reform body, stating at a cabinet meeting that "police appear to be exercising the greatest power among state institutions." The Democratic Party hastily launched a police reform task force. However, it was the government and ruling party that implemented "complete prosecutorial investigation ban," granting police full investigative authority without prior verification of police investigative capacity and internal discipline, nor any oversight mechanisms. It is putting the cart before the horse to now demand reform by questioning police capability and lax discipline. This crisis was entirely foreseeable. The Democratic Party steamrolled through amendments to the criminal procedure law that completely strip prosecutors of investigative authority, ignoring concerns and opposition from legal circles, academia, and civil society. As a result, while entrusting all investigations to police, prosecutors were left without even supplementary investigative powers, eliminating any mechanisms to check and balance police abuse of authority. Ignoring warnings that the vulnerable would suffer, the fruits of this forcibly pursued legislation are the police negligence we now witness. What citizens want is not institutional change driven by political objectives, but everyday security from crime. While officials including the Jeju West Police Station chief have been reassigned over the false closure of the missing person case, holding station chiefs accountable should not be the end of it. The government and ruling party must reflect on the unintended consequences of unprepared criminal justice reforms, and while time remains, pursue substantial corrective legislation such as restoring prosecutors' supplementary investigative powers.

editorial.title: Police bury cases
editorial.body: Arbitrary closure of missing persons cases raises concerns about police monopoly on investigations Given the recent police misconduct involving officers quietly burying cases at an early stage, having suspects treated as witnesses, and helping to destroy key evidence, it is astonishing that the police can still claim to be on the front line of public safety. With the revised Criminal Procedure Act set to take effect on Oct. 2, public anxiety over the police’s impending monopoly over investigative authority is bound to grow. A police officer at Jeju Seobu Police Station in Jeju City, who is accused of deceiving the family of 37-year-old Jang Mi-ran and falsely closing her missing person case, has been found to have deliberately mishandled another missing person case in the same fashion. On Saturday, police were searching for Jang after discovering her case was closed prematurely and found the body of a man whose disappearance had been first reported to police 51 days earlier. On July 2, the police officer who falsely closed Jang's case received a missing person report from the man's family. Shortly afterward, he reportedly lied to the family that he had contacted the man. The officer said that the man was safe but did not want his family to know his whereabouts, and then the officer closed the case. After seeing news reports about Jang's disappearance, the missing man's family again reported his disappearance to police, who later found him dead in the Jeju City area during their search. Jang is said to have left her home in Hallim-eup, Jeju City, in the early hours of May 13, after which she became unreachable. The same officer, who was on night duty when he received the report that she was missing on May 15, told his superior that he had made contact with her and closed the case that day. Still, Jang remained out of contact with her family, who filed another missing person report in July. The police have resumed the search, but now, three months after her disappearance, CCTV footage from the area where she was last seen has been deleted, making it difficult to trace her movements. The early closure of the case cost police the golden window for investigating her disappearance. No record of the phone call with Jang, as claimed by the police officer, has been found, raising suspicions that the claim was fabricated. The police officer also deleted Jang's case record from the Missing Person Profiling System at his own discretion. The system is an internal police information network that tracks missing person reports, search efforts and results, as well as the grounds for closing cases. The notion that a single police officer can unilaterally decide the fate of a case involving citizens' lives is simply unacceptable. The cases might have been solved if the police had responded promptly at the outset and launched investigations immediately after the two disappearances were reported. Moreover, the truth about the cases only began to emerge after the families of the missing persons publicized their disappearances on social media. In Seoul, the head of the investigation team at Gangnam Police Station was arrested and indicted on suspicion of helping bury a case by having a suspect treated as a witness. The officer allegedly did so at the request of the husband of a well-known Pilates instructor who had been accused of fraud. In the murder of a high school girl in Gwangju, the father of the killer, an active-duty police officer, obtained confidential investigation information and used it to destroy key evidence. It is hard not to despair when police officers like this will be entrusted with full investigative authority. The dysfunction in the investigative system shows that similar instances could occur anywhere and at any time. If this is how police investigations are being handled even now, it is frightening to imagine what may happen after Oct. 2, when prosecutors lose their power to conduct supplementary investigations and the police come to monopolize investigative authority. It could be a lot worse than falsely closing a missing persons case. 경찰의 자의적인 실종 사건 종결에 우려 커져…수사권 독점 문제 대두

최근 경찰의 비위 사건들—초기 단계에서 사건을 은폐하고, 용의자를 참고인으로 처우하며, 핵심 증거 은폐를 돕는 행태—을 감안할 때, 경찰이 여전히 공공 안전의 최전선에 서 있다고 주장할 수 있다는 것은 놀라울 따름이다. 10월 2일 시행될 개정 형사소송법을 앞두고, 경찰의 수사권 독점에 대한 국민의 불안감은 더욱 커질 수밖에 없을 것이다.

제주시 제주 서부경찰서의 한 경찰관이 37세의 장미란씨 가족을 기만해 실종 신고를 거짓으로 종결한 혐의를 받고 있는데, 동일한 방식으로 다른 실종 사건을 의도적으로 은폐한 것으로 드러났다. 토요일 경찰이 장씨 사건이 조기에 종결된 사실을 발견한 후 수색에 나선 결과, 51일 전 경찰에 실종 신고된 남성의 시신을 발견했다. 7월 2일 장씨 사건을 거짓으로 종결한 경찰관이 그 남성의 가족으로부터 실종 신고를 받았다. 직후 그는 해당 남성과 연락했다고 거짓 진술한 뒤, 남성이 안전하지만 가족에게 행방을 알리고 싶지 않다고 말했고, 그 후 사건을 종결했다. 장씨 실종 관련 언론 보도를 본 그 남성의 가족이 다시 경찰에 실종 신고를 했고, 경찰은 수색 과정에서 제주시 지역에서 그를 사망한 상태로 발견했다.

장씨는 5월 13일 새벽 제주시 한림읍 자신의 집을 나간 후 연락이 두절된 것으로 알려졌다. 5월 15일 실종 신고를 받을 당시 야간 근무 중이던 같은 경찰관은 상급자에게 본인이 장씨와 연락했다고 보고한 뒤 그날 사건을 종결했다. 그러나 장씨는 여전히 가족과 연락이 두절된 상태였고, 가족은 7월에 다시 실종 신고를 했다. 경찰은 수색을 재개했지만, 실종 이후 3개월이 지난 현재 장씨가 마지막으로 목격된 지역의 CCTV 영상이 삭제되어 행적을 추적하기 어렵게 되었다. 조기 종결로 인해 경찰은 실종 사건 수사의 황금 시간을 놓쳤다. 경찰관이 주장한 장씨와의 통화 기록은 발견되지 않았으며, 이는 그 주장이 조작되었을 가능성을 높이고 있다. 해당 경찰관은 또한 실종자프로파일링시스템에서 장씨 사건 기록을 자의로 삭제했다. 이 시스템은 실종 신고, 수색 활동 및 결과, 그리고 사건 종결의 근거를 추적하는 경찰 내부 정보망이다.

단 한 명의 경찰관이 일반인의 생명과 관련된 사건의 운명을 일방적으로 결정할 수 있다는 생각은 단순히 받아들일 수 없다. 경찰이 초기부터 신속하게 대응했고 두 실종 신고 직후 수사를 즉시 개시했다면 사건이 해결되었을 가능성이 크다. 더욱이 사건의 진실은 실종자 가족들이 소셜 미디어를 통해 실종 사실을 공개한 이후에야 드러나기 시작했다.

서울의 강남경찰서 수사팀장은 사기 혐의를 받은 유명 필라테스 강사의 남편 요청에 따라 용의자를 참고인으로 처우해 사건을 은폐한 혐의로 체포되어 기소되었다. 광주의 고등학생 살인 사건에서는 가해자인 현직 경찰관의 아버지가 수사 기밀 정보를 입수해 핵심 증거를 은폐하는 데 이용했다. 이런 경찰관들이 완전한 수사권을 행사하게 될 것이라 생각하면 절망하지 않을 수 없다.

수사 시스템의 기능 부전은 유사한 사건이 언제든 어디서든 발생할 수 있음을 보여준다. 지금도 경찰 수사가 이런 식으로 진행되고 있다면, 10월 2일 이후 검찰이 보충 수사권을 잃고 경찰이 수사권을 독점하게 될 때 어떤 일이 벌어질지는 상상하기 두렵다. 단순한 실종 사건 종결 조작보다 훨씬 심각할 수 있다.

editorials.title: Police bury cases
editorials.body: Arbitrary closure of missing persons cases raises concerns about police monopoly on investigations Given the recent police misconduct involving officers quietly burying cases at an early stage, having suspects treated as witnesses, and helping to destroy key evidence, it is astonishing that the police can still claim to be on the front line of public safety. With the revised Criminal Procedure Act set to take effect on Oct. 2, public anxiety over the police’s impending monopoly over investigative authority is bound to grow. A police officer at Jeju Seobu Police Station in Jeju City, who is accused of deceiving the family of 37-year-old Jang Mi-ran and falsely closing her missing person case, has been found to have deliberately mishandled another missing person case in the same fashion. On Saturday, police were searching for Jang after discovering her case was closed prematurely and found the body of a man whose disappearance had been first reported to police 51 days earlier. On July 2, the police officer who falsely closed Jang's case received a missing person report from the man's family. Shortly afterward, he reportedly lied to the family that he had contacted the man. The officer said that the man was safe but did not want his family to know his whereabouts, and then the officer closed the case. After seeing news reports about Jang's disappearance, the missing man's family again reported his disappearance to police, who later found him dead in the Jeju City area during their search. Jang is said to have left her home in Hallim-eup, Jeju City, in the early hours of May 13, after which she became unreachable. The same officer, who was on night duty when he received the report that she was missing on May 15, told his superior that he had made contact with her and closed the case that day. Still, Jang remained out of contact with her family, who filed another missing person report in July. The police have resumed the search, but now, three months after her disappearance, CCTV footage from the area where she was last seen has been deleted, making it difficult to trace her movements. The early closure of the case cost police the golden window for investigating her disappearance. No record of the phone call with Jang, as claimed by the police officer, has been found, raising suspicions that the claim was fabricated. The police officer also deleted Jang's case record from the Missing Person Profiling System at his own discretion. The system is an internal police information network that tracks missing person reports, search efforts and results, as well as the grounds for closing cases. The notion that a single police officer can unilaterally decide the fate of a case involving citizens' lives is simply unacceptable. The cases might have been solved if the police had responded promptly at the outset and launched investigations immediately after the two disappearances were reported. Moreover, the truth about the cases only began to emerge after the families of the missing persons publicized their disappearances on social media. In Seoul, the head of the investigation team at Gangnam Police Station was arrested and indicted on suspicion of helping bury a case by having a suspect treated as a witness. The officer allegedly did so at the request of the husband of a well-known Pilates instructor who had been accused of fraud. In the murder of a high school girl in Gwangju, the father of the killer, an active-duty police officer, obtained confidential investigation information and used it to destroy key evidence. It is hard not to despair when police officers like this will be entrusted with full investigative authority. The dysfunction in the investigative system shows that similar instances could occur anywhere and at any time. If this is how police investigations are being handled even now, it is frightening to imagine what may happen after Oct. 2, when prosecutors lose their power to conduct supplementary investigations and the police come to monopolize investigative authority. It could be a lot worse than falsely closing a missing persons case. editorials.titleTr: Editorial: Time to crack down on tax evasion schemes exploiting imperial residences
summaryTr: Authorities have identified 50 companies whose executives and their families have used corporate-owned luxury homes as if they were personal residences.
According to a tax investigation by the National Tax Service, the suspected tax evasion amounts to 1.9 trillion won.
The practice of illegally converting company housing and condominiums for exclusive use by chairmen must be eradicated.
editorials.bodyTr: Fifty companies that allowed their executives and their families to use expensive properties registered under corporate names as if they were personal residences have become targets of tax investigation. The National Tax Service launched its probe on the 25th, and the suspected tax evasion amount revealed so far totals 1.9 trillion won. Company executives lived rent-free in corporate housing, while condominiums and vacation homes purchased for employee welfare became reserved for the chairman's exclusive use. The corporations deducted these as business expenses, and individuals paid nothing—a classic structure for evading taxes and social insurance contributions. This is not merely a matter of corporate misconduct. It represents a systematic exploitation of the tax system and raises questions about whether our tax authorities have been sufficiently vigilant. The fact that such schemes persisted at dozens of major corporations without detection suggests significant blind spots in the current oversight system. The investigation must move beyond simple penalty assessments and pursue criminal charges where warranted. Additionally, a comprehensive review of related regulations is necessary to close loopholes that have enabled such abuses. Only through thorough accountability can we restore faith in fair taxation.

The significantly lower adoption rate compared to developed nations threatens our technological competitive advantage.
This is a critical moment requiring active government support and regulatory easing.
